question: Quantify the DBI backend's per-syscall interception advantage over ptrace, and its fixed startup tax, so the perf lead is documented and regressions are detectable.

host.name: devbig014
host.load_during_run: ~61-93 (shared host; min-of-N used to suppress contention noise)

hermit.note: The --summary stats commit on this branch does not affect run performance; the ptrace binary and DBI backend are the same release binary.

method: min-of-3 wall-clock via /usr/bin/time -o FILE -f %e; guest stdout/stderr to /dev/null; ratio (not absolute) is the trustworthy signal on a loaded shared host

workloads.startup_tax: /bin/true (fixed backend attach/teardown cost, ~no guest syscalls of interest)
workloads.per_syscall: syscall_loop 100000 (tight raw SYS_getpid loop; every iteration crosses the backend)
workloads.branch_bound: branch_heavy 2000000 (sum of Collatz step counts over 1..2e6; ~745M counted branches, ~37 syscalls; syscall-free hot loop that isolates DBI per-branch translation cost)

ab_counter_variants.purpose: Test whether the unconditional per-branch DRX_COUNTER_LOCK counter in reverie-dbi/native/client.c (~line 815) is the DBI compute-slowness. Refuted.
ab_counter_variants.runtime_selector_env: REVERIE_DBI_CLIENT (launcher CLIENT_ENV; NOT HERMIT_DBI_CLIENT, which the launcher ignores)
ab_counter_variants.conclusion: Removing the lock, and removing the entire counter update, both yield NO speedup (within noise). The counter is not the bottleneck; DynamoRIO per-branch code-cache dispatch is. No reverie-dbi lock-removal PR is warranted on perf grounds.

results_branch_heavy_2e6_min_of_5_s.dbi_vs_ptrace: ~11x slower (structural DBI translation cost on syscall-free compute; ptrace runs pure compute at native speed)
